to students across the country of  world-class quality universal education with personalized learning 
experience at their doorsteps, recommends towards developing more such hubs and spoke models of 
education delivery. The Committee recommends that public universities can act as hubs with l ocal 
institutions serving as the spokes, and can thus become a carrier of quality education to all parts of the 
country. Further, the Committee recommends that a new Phygital or Physical plus Digital (hybrid) way of 
instructions be experimented with in a structured manner and its impact assessed scientifically. 
(Para 4) 
Action Taken 
 The Committee was informed that Government of India in its Budget 2022 -2023 has announced 
establishment of Digital University which is as follows: 
 
“A Digital University will b e established to provide access to students across the country for 
world-class quality universal education with personalised learning experience at their doorsteps. This will 
be made available in different Indian languages and ICT formats. The University w ill be built on a 
networked hub -spoke model, with the hub building cutting edge ICT expertise. The best public 
universities and institutions in the country will collaborate as a network of hub-spokes.” 
 
It was also informed that following collaborative models are also being worked out: 
• UGC has prepared a concept note on Blended mode of teaching and learning in Higher 
Educational Institutions, 2022 which allows HEIs to teach up to 40% of syllabus of each course 
(other than SWAYAM course) through online mode and the remaining 60% syllabus of the 
concerned courses is to be taught in offline mode. Examination for both 40% online and 60% 
offline teaching will be conducted offline.  
• IIMs conduct programmes for corporate executives/government officers and ex ecutives of 
other organizations in online/hybrid modes. Libraries in IIMs have digital access both for faculty 
and students which helps in providing learning experience at their doorstep. Apart from courses in 
physical mode, IIMs also conduct online mode o f classes and assessments by using different 
audio-visual technologies for smooth delivery of the curriculum. The Institutes also have high -end 
technology in the form of hybrid classrooms for conducting classes to both offline and online 
students at the same time seamlessly. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
  The Committee observes that the National Digital University (NDU) promises inclusive, 
flexible, and affordable education aligned with NEP goals. However, it foundation, SWAYAM, 
faces significant challenges. Since 2017, less than 4 per cent of enrolled students have completed 
SWAYAM courses. Complaints include outdated content, inflexible teaching, and poor 
infrastructure. Teachers report inadequate training, low compensation, and technical hurdles, 
undermining their efficiency. The 1:15 teacher -student ratio is disregarded in the online model, 
leading to overcrowded virtual classrooms. Additionally, only 4 per cent of SC/ST and 7 per cent of 
OBC students have internet -enabled computers, per Oxfam India 2022 , questioning NDU's equity 
claims. 
 The Committee feels that digital initiatives will only provide lukewarm response in terms of 
engagement unless the Department starts proactively assisting in placements wherever possible or 
establishing a platform associate d with SWAYAM for connecting recruiters to students. The 

18 
 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should also take steps to ensure courses 
are completed by candidates, since major private online platforms suffer from this. The 
Department should also consider establishing a separate cell for ensuring greater participation of 
students from underprivileged sections of society and should also monitor their enrolment and 
progress diligently. 
 
Recommendation

Recommendation  
 
8. The Committee notes that even after several decades, many State Universities regularly fail in 
smooth and flawless conduct of examinations. Instances like —  
a) Question paper leak  
b) Administering a wrong question paper 
c) Confusion about seating arrangements and Exam centre  
d) Rampant cases of copying  
e) Framing questions that are out of syllabi  
f) Wrong examiners being appointed for assessment; and  
g) Student-Examiner Nexus  
etc. are still not uncommon. Hence the Committee recommends that the Parameter of the Institution’s 
exam management competency be also considered as a 46 mandatory norm towards consideration of 
accreditation. The NAAC and NBA should award marks to such universities/institutes who conduct 
examinations smoothly. Besides, experiment s like the Question Bank system and adoption of complete 
digitization of the examination process by institutes/universities to ensure fair and timely conduct of 
examination and declaration of results, amongst others may be incentivised. 
(Para 9)

9. The Committee notes the need to carefully examine, assess and analyze the issues and challenges 
for NBA and NAAC, through compilation of a structured feedback of HEIs so that requisite reform 
process can be taken forward to make these bodies a benchmark for qu ality accreditation. Also, it is 
recommended that the norms for frequency and periodicity of the accreditations be defined so that 
institutions do not develop a tendency to carry the score for years, without a review, which leads to 
complacency, and undermines quality mechanisms.                (Para 10) 
 
Action Taken 
 
 The Department has informed that with regard to NAAC assessment and accreditation a 
Committee was constituted under the Chairpersonship of Dr. K. Radhakrishnan, Chairperson BoG, IIT 
Kanpur &  Chairperson, Standing Committee of IIT Council. The draft report of this Committee was 
placed in the public domain from 19 th May, 2023 to 22 nd June, 2023; later extended upto 15 th July, 2023 
and again from 8 th August, 2023 to 15 th August, 2023. Further, a s a part of stakeholder consultation, an 
Online Consultative Workshop on Reforms in Assessment, Accreditation and Ranking of HEIs was also 
held on 7 th July, 2023. After consideration of about 1450 feedback received from various categories of 
stakeholders on the draft report, the Committee submitted its final report on ‘Transformative Reforms for 
Strengthening Periodic Assessment and Accreditation of all HEIs in India’. The Committee has 
considered the introduction of strategic reforms consistent with the vi sion of the National Education 
Policy, 2020 and the need for adopting a simple, trust -based, objective and rationalized system for 
accreditation and ranking of HEIs with a verifiable and secured centralized database through technology -
driven systems. Metho dologies for facilitating Ease of Doing Business for the stakeholders, duly 
facilitating students in making more informed choices for selection of institutions/ programmes have also 
been considered by the Committee. The recommendations also focus on scheme s for raising the 
participation of HEIs as well as accreditation levels, towards eminence, significance and global acclaim.  
 
It was further informed that the recommendations made by the Dr. Radhakrishnan Committee 
have been accepted by the Ministry. The r eport is available on the website of the M/o Education at 
https://www.education.gov.in/sites/upload_files/mhrd/files/document-reports/reforms_moe.pdf . 
 
After acceptance of report, National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) in its 
meeting held on 27.01.2024 decided that Binary Accreditation for HEIs shall be implemented in the next 
four months and Maturity -Based Graded Accreditation by December, 2024. Methodologies and formats 
used in the assessment and accreditation process are already being redesigned using One Nation One Data 
platform. Implementation of binary accreditation is in line with NEP 2020 and as per global practices.  
 
The Department has also informed the Committee that to bring qualitative changes in examination 
system, AICTE came out with Bloom’s Taxonomy based exam reforms policy for technical institutions 
and is conducting workshops/ training programmes on Examination Reforms for Controllers of 
Examination, Deans and Senior Faculty members of various universities and institutions. The faculty 
trained through the workshops are expected to train faculty of their respective institutions. Question banks 
are being developed to prepare model question papers. 
 
Comments of the Committee  
The Committee notes the reply given by the Department regarding smooth and flawless 
conduct of examinations for avoiding instances such as Question paper leak, Administering a wrong 
question pap er, Confusion about seating arrangements and Exam centre, etc.  However, the 
Committee feels that still, there is an urgent need to address instances , especially Question paper 

27 
 
leak and administering a wrong question paper  etc. and therefore, the Committee observes that the 
reply of the Department should have also taken care of this aspect . Therefore, the Committee 
desires to be apprised of the reform process to be undertaken in addition to constitution of Dr.

accreditation and to address the issues as recommended by the Committee. 
Further, the Department should bring out the methodologies and formats used in the 
assessment and accreditation process which are already being redesigne d using One Nation One 
Data platform, so that, institutions do not develop a tendency to carry the score for years, without a 
review, which leads to complacency, and undermines quality mechanisms . In addition to this,

Action Taken 
  
 The Department has informed the Committee that Para 11.4 of NEP 2020 envisages HEIs to move 
towards more holistic and multidisciplinary education with more arts and humanities. Students of arts and 
humanities will aim to learn more science and all will make an effort to incorporate more vocational 
subjects and soft skills. Section 6 (1) (a) of the Institutes of Technology Act, 1961 already provides 
statutory power to IITs to be a multi -disciplinary institution. Most of the IITs are already offering courses 
in the stream of humanities and social sciences, ma y come up with more courses in line with the 
recommendation of NEP, 2020. IITs, which at present are confined to only engineering and science may 
think of starting programmes in other streams from the new academic session and build up capacities 
accordingly. Humanities are being taught as a course in most of the IITs since long.   
 
It was also informed that the Act and the Statutes of respective IIIT provide full autonomy to the 
Institute in their academic affairs including design course curriculum as per r equirement. AICTE with the 
help of industry -academia experts, has framed the curriculum for model curriculum for UG Level 
programmes and introduced Humanities and Social Sciences including Management courses provision of 
awarding minor degree in Universal Human Values (UHV) has been made for students who earn 18 -20 
credits in UHV. This will provide an opportunity to students to have a holistic worldview along with 
technical skills and they would strive to ensure value-based living for themselves as well as the society. 
 
Comments of the Committee  
 
The Committee  had recommended the incorporation of social sciences/ humanities/ arts 
modules in the technical education curriculum for the development of students with well -rounded 
personalities. But in the reply, the Department has mentioned only about IIT and IIIT, and there is 
no mention of other HEIs and various Institutions under State/UT Governments to provide holistic 
and multidisciplinary education . The Committee, therefore recommends that other HEIs should 
also include courses from  the stream of humanities and social sciences, and come up with more 
courses in line with the recommendations of NEP, 2020. 

28 
 
 
Recommendation  
11. Noting the growing commercialization of education in certain States and the disturbing  trend of 
many colleges associating with coaching classes to prepare their enrolled students in certain cities, 
making the learning process a farce through this unholy nexus between coaching classes and colleges, the 
Committee recommends that the Governmen t, in coordination with State Governments must work out 
mechanisms to curb such trends and punish such institutions by derecognizing them. Towards this end, 
the Committee recommends that a study group may be set up by the Central Government to assess the 
ground realities. 
(Para 15) 
Action Taken 
The Department has informed the Committee that the recommendation of the Committee has been 
noted. 
 
Comments of the Committee  
The Committee observers that  the Department has not taken any action against the 
recommendation of the Committee which categorically stat es that in view of growing 
commercialization of education in certain stat es and the disturbing trend of making the learning 
process a farce through unh oly nexus between coaching classes and colleges, mechanism to curb 
such trends and to punish such institutions by  derecognizing them is inevitable for sake of quality 
education and students. The Committee had further recommended for setting up of study gro ups 
by the Central Government t o assess the ground realities . However, the Department is silent about 
the action taken, so far, in this regard. 
 
The Committee therefore, reiterates that Department should proactively  identity and  take 
action against those colleges which have nexus with coaching classes and derecognize these colleges.  
Further, the Committee recommends  for setting up of a study group by Central Government in 
time bound manner, so that this evil can be eradicated from root and to apprise the Committee in 
this regard.  
 
Recommendation  
12. While the increasing usage of cutting edge technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine 
Learning, Robotics, Virtual Reality etc. is welcome for several reasons, the Committee recommends that a 
task force should be set up at central level to explore the possibility of incorporating these new emerging 
49 technologies in contemporary syllabi and develop them for increasing the employment opportunities. 
(Para 25) 
Action Taken 
 The Department has informed the Committee that AICTE is approving B.Tech Programme in Data 
Science and Artificial Intelligence and encouraging technical Institutions to introduce new emerging 
technologies in course curriculum of traditional disciplines also. Through ATAL Academy, it is imparting 
training to faculty members on new emerging technologies under Faculty Development Programme. It 
will extend its cooperation to the proposed Task Force, as suggested.

Comments of the Committee  
 
The Committee takes note of the Action Taken Note furnished by the Department and 
expresses its anguish over the fact that response given therein against the recommendation to set up 
task force for incorporating e merging technologies in contemporary syllabi to increase the 
employment opportunities is not satisfactory .  The Committee, th erefore, recommends to set up 
Task Force as stated earlier and furnish a status Note o n progress made thereon for perusal and 
consideration of the Committee.

RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE -AT A GLANCE 
 
 
1. The Committee observes that the multiplicity of regulators leads to inconsistency in 
standards and monitoring, making it difficult for institutions to function effectively. Moreover, 
State Universities, which educate over 90 per cent of the student populat ion, are caught in between 
national and state -level regulations. The draft Higher Education Commission of India Bill (HECI) 
(which seeks to replace UGC as a single regulator) appears to perpetuate many of these same issues 
by maintaining a Central Governme nt- heavy composition and insufficient State representation. 
The proposed HECI Bill will hold significant power, including the ability to grant degree -awarding 
authority and close institutions failing to meet standards. This removes State control and could lead 
to the closure of institutions in rural areas that suffer from infrastructure or faculty shortages. It 
would indirectly fuel privatization especially in rural areas . The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that a simplified hierarchy of regulatory bodie s would be more effective, the 
Department should ensure that any such unified regulatory body must have adequate 
representation for all States and there should not be excess centralization.  
 (Para 2) 
 
2. The Committee observes that the Department in its A ction Taken Note has emphasized on 
several initiatives aimed at skill development which includes linkages with industry and institutions, 
summits and leadership workshops, entrepreneurship centres at business schools. However, these 
initiatives focus only on certain fraction of students who have commerce or science or technical 
background. It ignores students with humanity related subjects. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Department should emphasize more on students from non -technical, 
humanities and related backgrounds. There should be opportunities in institutes to bring in 
expertise of established persons of a field. For instance, established writers, storytellers propagating 
writing skills as a potential career option. Similarly, there shou ld be increased field visits for 
students enrolled in archaeology, geology, etc. Further, the Ministry should also take initiatives to 
generate awareness on further career/ education opportunities in these fields and collaborate with 
other Ministries to provide associated opportunities.  
(Para 3) 
 
3. The Committee observes that the National Digital University (NDU) promises inclusive, 
flexible, and affordable education aligned with NEP goals. However, it foundation, SWAYAM, 
faces significant challenges. Since 2017, less than 4 per cent of enrolled students have completed 
SWAYAM courses. Complaints include outdated content, inflexible teaching, and poor 
infrastructure. Teachers report inadequate training, low compensation, and technical hurdles, 
undermining their efficiency. The 1:15 teacher -student ratio is disregarded in the online model, 
leading to overcrowded virtual classrooms. Additionally, only 4 per cent of SC/ST and 7 per cent of 
OBC students have internet -enabled computers, per Oxfam India 2022, q uestioning NDU's equity 
claims. 
 The Committee feels that digital initiatives will only provide lukewarm response in terms of 
engagement unless the Department starts proactively assisting in placements wherever possible or 
establishing a platform associate d with SWAYAM for connecting recruiters to students. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should also take steps to ensure courses 
are completed by candidates, since major private online platforms suffer from this. The 
Department should also consider establishing a separate cell for ensuring greater participation of 

32 
 
students from underprivileged sections of society and should also monitor their enrolment and 
progress diligently. 
(Para 4) 
 
4.  The Committee notes the work done by the Ministry and the IIMs in particular in this 
regard. However, the Ministry should work to ensure that Section 35 of the Income Tax Act 
provide 100% deduction of payment made to the IITs /National Universities not jus t for scientific 
research purposes but for all purposes – as recommended by the Committee, to ensure maximum 
mobilization of funds for central universities.  
(Para 5) 
5. The Committee notes the Ministry’s attempts to secure adequate talent for our higher 
educational institutes. However, action should be taken on the Committee’s specific 
recommendation on appointing talented alumni/senior students/Ph.D. scholars as Teaching 
Assistants. It can be done on a trial basis in a few universities and evaluated befo re being scaled up 
nationally. Finally, the Committee also directs the Department to share the report of the Expert 
Committee and its Membership at the earliest. 
 The Committee further observes that most universities especially under the Central 
Government have a higher amount of contractual workforce. As many as four thousand teachers 
are employed in Central Universities in temporary posts. This shift away from permanent, secure 
government jobs towards casual, short-term contracts has been driven by the Go vernment's retreat 
from public education and the increasing influence of neo -liberal policies. Contractual positions 
offer no job security, no salary increments, and lack of social security benefits like promotions, 
pensions, or paid leave. Despite, these disadvantages, such jobs have become highly sought after due 
to the scarcity of permanent jobs, particularly in fields like social sciences and humanities. 
Contractual faculties also face institutional hurdles when attempting to conduct research, including  
lack of access to research grants and insufficient institutional recognition. The Committee, 
therefore, strongly recommends that the Department should work on regularization of jobs to 
provide job security and ensure fair working conditions as well to enh ance capacity building which 
will motivate them to put effort for improving research and pedagogy. 
 
 (Para 6 and 8) 
 
 
   
6. The Committee acknowledges the Department's efforts to secure international collaboration 
in higher education. However, more can be done on this front. For instance, according to the

travel assistance and registration fees to students. Department should also amend the scheme to

Children, Youth and Sports deals with the action taken by the Government on the

CHAPTER-I 
RECOMMENDATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT 
Recommendation  
1. The Committee appreciates the manner in which the implementation of NEP and the vision it 
espouses is being taken forward by the UT of Jammu and Kashmir. The Committee notes that the UT of 
J&K is one of the first in the country to implement NEP 2020 from the academic session 2022 in all the 
Higher Education Institutions. It also notes that it has been at the forefront in implementing NEP by 
bringing significant changes in the assessment system from rote learning to a competency based learning. 
Also, a paradigm shift in the methods of teaching in class room to learn from surroundings in order to 
give holistic and lifelong learning opportunities to students is being witnessed across J&K which will 
ensure sustained training of students as global citizens with 21st century skills and create a vibrant, 
innovative, practical and vocational skill set and research-oriented, learner-centric education system in 
our country. 
 (Para 4.10.2 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
2. The Committee is pleased to note that the University of Jammu has recently been designated as the 
nodal University by the University Grants Commission (UGC) to spearhead the implementation of the 
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir as this distinction 
brings great pride and honour to the institution. Noting that the University of Jammu has been entrusted 
with the pivotal responsibility of executing the mandates set forth in the NEP, along with various 
recommendations and regulations outlined by the UGC, the Committee hopes that with this new role, the 
University of Jammu will be able play a central role in creating awareness, arranging programs, and 
offering guidance to higher education institutions within Jammu and Kashmir to effectively implement 
NEP, thereby providing a platform to exchange and adopt best practices.  
(Para 4.10.3 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 Appreciation on the action taken by UT of J&K and University of Jammu is respectfully noted. 
 
Recommendation  
3. The Committee appreciates the steady progress in the field of higher education. The Committee 
recommends that the specific impetus is required to be assigned to factors which can help the country’s 
ranking in patent filing. Though the overall patent filing has improved significantly but more needs to be 
done by enhanced allocation for Anusandhan (Research). 
(Para 4.10.7 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 One of the principles of NEP 2020 is to develop culture of research and innovation in India HEIs. 
In order to achieve the global standard of quality and to foster the culture of research and innovation, 
several initiatives have been taken such as establishment of Research & Development Cell and 
Institution’s Innovation Councils (IIC) in the campus of HEIs which will enable attainment of targets of 
Atma-Nirbhar Bharat and is expected to play a pivotal role in catalysing multidisciplinary/ trans-
disciplinary and translational research culture. Around 2500 HEIs and 300 Universities have established 
R&D Cells at their campuses and 14518 IICs have been set up in 28 States and 9 UTs.   
IDEA Labs (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) are also being set up for promoting 
multidisciplinary education & research, strong societal and industry linkage, new age learning and

encouraging STEM, experiential learning among faculty members and students. Around 113 HEIs funded 
for IDEA labs.  
Filing of patents increased by more than 93.65% in since 2014-15, rising to 82,811 in 2023 from 
42,763 in 2014 (IPO Annual Reports). 
Total Number of patents filed by Educational Institutes has risen to 19,430 in 2022-23 from 7501 
in 2021-22, which is an increase of around 159%.  
Number of patents filed by HEIs constitutes 23% of total patents filed.  
IITs collectively tops with 803 patent applications. 
CAR-T Cell Therapy - accessible & affordable cancer therapy has been developed by IITB & Tata 
Memorial Hospital in association with industry partner with Immune ACT and inaugurated on April 04, 
2024. 
Furthermore, under the Start-Up Indian Initiative in Higher Educational Institutions, Research 
Parks are being established at IITs. These Research Parks act as a focal point for Research and Incubation 
activities. 
Recommendation  
4. The Committee appreciates that the freedom being given to Indian universities to set up campuses 
in other countries and initiate start-up incubation centers, technology development centers and centers in 
frontier areas of research helps foster knowledge creation and innovation which will contribute to the 
growing national economy. In this regard the Committee also takes note of G20 New Delhi declarations 
that supported promoting open, equitable, and secure scientific collaboration and encouraging mobility 
of students, scholars, researchers and scientists across research and higher education institutions. The 
Declaration also emphasized on expanding access to high-quality technical and vocational education and 
training. The Committee is of the view that the expected benefits through these initiatives call for 
commitment of all stakeholders, be it the Department, regulatory bodies or Universities, educationists, 
and industries, so that, these innovative strategies in the areas of skill development, up-skilling and 
entrepreneurship bring the expected boost to create a knowledge society that contributes to global 
education, hence global good. The Committee further recommends that efforts, in unison, by both the 
Central and State Governments, would be necessary for successful implementation and sustenance of 
these policies and schemes. 
(Para 4.10.9 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 NEP 2020 envisions an education system rooted in Indian ethos that contributes directly to 
transforming India, that is Bharat, sustainably into an equitable and vibrant knowledge society, by 
providing high-quality education to all, and thereby making India a global knowledge superpower.  
NEP 2020 also envisions making the education student-centric. This is expected to be achieved by 
providing students with opportunities for multi-disciplinary and flexible education which gives them the 
ability to transition across courses as per their requirements. 
In order to enable HEIs to work with industry experts in developing courses and curriculum to 
meet the industry and societal needs, initiatives have been taken such as Guidelines on Professor of 
Practice; MoUs with Cisco/IBM/Meta/Adobe/Microsoft/Sales force etc. to create industry-aligned 
courses; offering Apprenticeship / Internship embedded Degree Programme by HEIs; Single Unified 
online portal for internship with total registration of around 10578 HEIs and 75585 industries so far. For 

4 
 
promotion of research and innovation, around 14518 Institutions’ Innovation Councils and around 113 
Idea Development, Evaluation and Application Labs (IDEA) have been set up. 
Recommendation  
5. Noting that the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 initiates several significant reforms to 
transform higher education in the country by promoting quality, relevance, and innovation in higher 
education, the Committee appreciates the various steps to promote the use of digital technologies in 
education, including the development of digital libraries& SWAYAM PRABHA portal. It is of the view 
that the recommendation for the creation of a National Educational Technology Forum (NETF) to equip 
students with the skills and knowledge necessary to contribute to the nation’s development and compete in 
the global job market can go a long way in expansion of digital infrastructure to make the country a 
Global Knowledge Hub thereby enhancing domain area of digital infrastructure, content and capacity 
building. 
 (Para 4.10.10 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
The foundation of the NEP 2020 framework rests upon ensuring education of high quality that is 
both affordable and accessible, while also promoting equity and accountability. The recommendations 
within NEP aim to revamp the regulatory structure, propelling India’s progression towards becoming a 
‘Global Knowledge Superpower’.  
The National Educational Technology Forum (NETF) operates as a specialized unit dedicated to 
e-Education. Its primary focus is to enhance digital infrastructure, develop digital content, and facilitate 
capacity building. By creating multilingual learning materials in various Indian regional languages and 
providing online technology solutions tailored to individual learner preferences, NETF aims to remove 
language and location barriers.  
NETF endeavours to establish an educational products and services marketplace. This platform 
will foster the exchange of ideas regarding technology’s role in improving learning, assessment, planning, 
and administration for School Education, Higher Education, and Skilling Initiatives. 
NETF aims to fulfil several pivotal roles within the Education Ecosystem, including serving as an 
advisor on critical issues aligned with NEP guidelines. Acting as a Think Tank, it will advise both the 
central and state governments on utilizing emerging technologies to achieve the goals set out by NEP 
2020. Additionally, it will facilitate the planning and execution of NEP objectives, oversee the 
fundamental components/modules of NDEAR (National Digital Education Architecture), and manage the 
adoption and lifecycle of educational digital infrastructure. Furthermore, it will take charge of the 
Operations & Maintenance of ongoing initiatives under larger educational schemes like NMEICT and 
DIKSHA.  
Recommendation  
6. The Committee observes that there is going to be significant impact of Digital Libraries on 
Knowledge Ecosystem as part of the NEP’s digitization agenda, digital libraries will play a crucial role 
in providing online access to an extensive range of digital resources, such as e-books, journals, articles, 
and multimedia content. These online platforms will enable students and educators to conveniently 
connect with educational materials at any time and from any location, while also offering a cost-effective 
means of providing the permit to top-notch educational content. The committee recommends that the 
department must ensure that the content on digital library should also be available in regional languages 
for better reach out and learning outcome.  
 (Para 4.10.11 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 

5 
 
Action Taken 
 Taking forward National Education Policy’s digitization agenda The National Digital Library of 
India (NDLI) stands as a flagship initiative under the National Mission on Education through Information 
and Communication Technology (NMEICT) Project, crafted by the Indian Institute of Technology 
Kharagpur in collaboration with the Ministry of Education. Functioning as a comprehensive repository, 
NDLI is an invaluable asset benefiting students, scholars, and enthusiastic learners, offering a diverse 
array of digital resources encompassing books, articles, journals, and educational videos. By 
consolidating digitized and digital content from various educational institutions nationwide, NDLI 
furnishes a unified platform facilitating e-learning. Its scope extends to delivering educational materials in 
multiple languages, across all academic disciplines, accessible through various devices, with plans in the 
pipeline to accommodate learners with different abilities.  
Presently, NDLI’s user interface accommodates English and ten additional Indian languages, 
including Hindi, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Telugu, among others, with ongoing efforts to 
incorporate more languages into its interface.  
Further, an initiative i.e. e-KUMBH (Knowledge Unleashed in Multiple Bhartiya Languages) 
Portal has been launched by AICTE. It is a repository of Engineering Books in different Indian 
Languages. 
Also Bhartiya Bhasha Sansthan is developing App named “Bhasha Sagar’ for language learning 
(270 Indian languages). 
Recommendation  
7. The Committee recommends that the Department and related stakeholders should prioritize the 
implementation of digital initiatives to ensure that every student, regardless of their background or 
location, has reach to quality education. In addition, policies that encourage the adoption of digital 
technologies in education should be framed, and both students and teachers should be provided adequate 
training for their use. 
 (Para 4.10.12 of the 356th Report of the Committee)

 Dedicated efforts for student learning support have been undertaken by NCERT such as 
ePathshala portal (https://epathshala.nic.in/) and mobile app platform to provide free access to the

audio format (https://ciet.nic.in/pages.php?id=audiobook&ln=en&ln=en). Supplementary reading material 
has also been developed by NCERT. 
In order to promote digital learning by leveraging technology, at present, 95 HEIs are offering 
1149 ODL programmes and 78 Higher Educational Institutions are offering 544 online programmes. 
More than 19 lakh students are availing these facilities.  
Technology enabled Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) based Solutions for Governance of HEIs 
starting from admission to grant of Degree – Smarter Automation Engine for Universities (SAMARTH) is 
being extensively used by   around 5300 Universities & HEIs covering 32 States/UTs. 7 State Higher 
Education Departments are also on boarded. In addition, The National Digital Library of India (NDLI) is 
providing e-learning content in form of books, articles, journals and educational videos in English and ten 
additional Indian languages including Hindi, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Telugu among others 
to provide excess to quality education to students from every part of the country.

11. The Committee observes that implementation of the Multi Entry and Multiple Exit (MEME) 
options within the framework of the National Education Policy (NEP) is a vital component of NEP 2020, 
offering students greater flexibility and choice in their educational pathways. In order to ensure its 
smooth operation, the Committee recommends that the Department should develop comprehensive 
guidelines and a well-defined framework for MEME options including specific eligibility criteria, credit 
transfer mechanisms providing clear roadmap for students pursuing different exit points. Also, 
implementation of a standardized Credit Accumulation and Transfer (CAT) system that allows students to 
earn and transfer credits seamlessly across institutions would facilitate smooth transitions between 
different levels of education, from certificate courses to doctoral programs. In this regard the Committee 
appreciates the introduction of Academic Bank of Credit (ABC) in the higher education system. It is 
commendable that already more than 50% of the Universities in the country are now on- board. The 
Committee recommends the Department to strive for bringing on-board the remaining Universities and 
other Higher Education Institutions of the country under Academic Bank of Credit. 
(Para 4.10.20 of  the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 Guidelines for Multiple Entry and Exit in Academic Programmes offered in the HEIs issued on 
28.07.2021, Regulation on Academic Bank of Credit issued on 28.07.2021 and further amended on 
28.12.2021, National Credit Framework (NCrF) released on 10.04.2023, National Higher Education 
Qualification Framework (NHEQF) released on 11.05.2023, Guidelines for Transforming Higher 
Education Institutions into Multidisciplinary Institutions issued on 02.09.2022  and Curriculum and

provides a framework for  multi-disciplinary holistic education at the undergraduate level with 
imaginative and flexible curricular structures, creative combinations of study, integration of vocational 
education, enabling education system, that nurtures and optimises individual potentials, provides multiple 
pathways and learning trajectories, lifelong learning etc. 
For Operationalisation of National Credit Framework (NCrF) in Higher Education, Standard 
Operating Procedure (SoP) has been issued.  The SOPs provides a clear guideline to facilitate the 
assignment, accumulation, storage, transfer, and redemption of such credits across school, higher, and 
vocational education and training and also advocates for multiple entry and exit points, recognition of 
prior learning, and work-embedded programs, enabling learners to acquire skills that integrate smoothly 
into formal education. The SOPs will empower educational institutions to serve as hubs for skill 
development, offering diverse learning pathways for students. 
2157 HEIs have onboarded ABC platform and more than 30 crore students have created 
APAARIDs on ABC platform to avail its benefits.

Action Taken 
 To widen the scope of HEFA, the existing Window structure has been modified and all types of 
institutions, including IIMs and IIIT (PPP), have been brought under the scope of HEFA.  
HEFA has been mandated to mobilise the fund from the market as per the actual requirements 
through debt from financial institutions and equity from the market. Depending upon the requirement, 
HEFA borrow money from the financial institutions like Public Sector Banks from time to time.  
In order to hand hold the institution in formulating the DPR for creation of infrastructure, HEFA 
has established a dedicated PMU which will help the institution in preparation of the DPR.

16. The Committee takes note of the fact that banks cannot enforce SARFAESI Act in case of default 
by borrower as same may jeopardize the careers of students (As per the submission given by the banks). 
The Committee, recommends that banks must take note of the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for 
Education Loan (CGFSEL) launched by the Department of Higher Education, Govt. of India in 2015 
which provides a guarantee of education loan up to INR 7.5 lakhs. The Committee also recommends that 

11 
 
the Ministry of Education in consultation with the Ministry of Finance should look into a proposal to 
increase the guarantee amount under this scheme. 
(Para 4.10.30 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 The “Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Education Loans (CGFSEL)” was notified on 
16.09.2015. Under the CGFSEL, Central Government gives guarantee for the education loans availed by 
students without any collateral security and third-party guarantee for a maximum loan limit of Rs. 7.5 
Lakh. The Fund provides guarantee cover to the extent of 75% of the amount in default through the 
National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Ltd. (NCGTC). For this, the banks disbursing education 
loans need to register them with the NCGTC as per scheme guidelines. 
New Initiative: To spread out reach of the scheme, Department of Higher Education vide notification 
dated 18.04.2023, has included 27 Regional Rural Banks under the scheme.

CHAPTER-III 
RECOMMENDATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE GOVERNMENT HAVE 
NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
 
Recommendation  
1. The Committee observes that through various appreciable activities, the implementation of the 
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 is progressing on course which would surely fructify its vision to 
transform the higher education system to be more inclusive, flexible, and aligned with global standards. 
The Committee notes that one of the primary keys to ensure successful implementation of NEP would be 
synergized collaboration between Government bodies, universities, industry partners, and civil society.  
(Para 4.10.1 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 Education being in the concurrent list of Constitution, Centre and States are equally responsible 
for providing quality education to all. To discuss innovative ideas for NEP implementation, a series of 
workshops / consultation-cum-review meetings have been held with States/UTs from time to time and 
also implementation of NEP 2020 was discussed in National Education Ministers' Conference held in 
Gujarat in June 2022; National Conference of Chief Secretaries held in June 2022; 7th Governing Council 
Meeting of NITI Aayog held in August 2022; Akhil Bharatiya Shiksha Samagam 2022, 2023 and 2024 
etc.  
National Workshop on Higher and Technical Education with the Secretaries of States / UTs 
covering various themes of NEP, 2020 was organised on 12th and 13th November 2024 in New Delhi 
NEP, 2020 inter-alia stipulates implementation of various aims, objects and goals with the active 
participation of stakeholders viz. local community, social workers, counsellors, educators, NGOs, peers 
and parents, senior citizens, students, alumni, principals, serving and retired faculty & teachers, 
vocational experts, local artists, industry, philanthropic organisations etc. 
In order to facilitate the universities to develop a road map for the effective implementation of 
NEP 2020, UGC has constituted five zonal Committees (Southern, Northern, Western, North Eastern and 
Eastern and Central Zone) having Vice Chancellors of Central Universities, State Universities, Private 
Universities and Deemed to be Universities. The Committees coordinate with HEIs of the Zones and 
guide them to adopt various initiatives for qualitative transformation of higher education, deliberate upon 
the strategies for implementation of NEP and challenges therein and share best practices. 
So far, VC’s conferences have been conducted in Western, Northern, Southern zone and Central 
Zone. As a special case, a conference was held at IIM Jammu, Jammu, on 23.2.2024 specifically for the 
UTs of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh. 
Several initiatives have been taken for implementation of NEP 2020 to revamp the School 
Education as well as Higher Education system have been appreciated and widely accepted by the States / 
UTs, Schools / Colleges / Universities / HEIs. 
Further recommendation of the Committee 
The Committee has observed that a “synergized collaboration” between stakeholders is 
required for the successful implementation of the NEP. In response, the Ministry has rightly noted 
that Education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution. It is therefore critical to have the 
complete confidence of the States to successfully advance the vision of the NEP. However, the 

14 
 
Ministry’s answer has not touched on the modalities as to how the Union Government is working 
with State Governments that have expressed reservations about various elements of the NEP in 
Higher Education. Hence, the Committee is of the opinion that the Ministry must develop a 
mechanism to coordinate with the States on any such concerns that they may have shared.  
The Committee desires that the Ministry should share a report of the Zonal Committee’s 
operations, including the Conferences held in various zones, with the Committee. 
The Committee recommends that a centralized nationwide tracker at the university-level 
should be developed to track progress on NEP implementation in higher education.  
Recommendation  
2. The Committee takes note and appreciates the introduction of “Design Your Degree” based on 
Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) launched by Jammu University under which students will be offered 
an opportunity to craft a personalized, interdisciplinary learning experience. The Committee further 
observes that “Design Your Degree” will also be introduced in Kashmir University, IUST Awantipora, 
ICSC Srinagar, GCW Parade Jammu, which is commendable. The Committee, therefore, recommends 
that the Department should take initiatives for introduction of “Design Your Degree” programme in 
various other HEIs in the country, as a model contemporary and futuristic in the interest of the student 
community and nation readiness. It will enable the students to craft a personalized, interdisciplinary 
learning experience.  
(Para 4.10.4 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 One of the fundamental principles of the National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020) is 
flexibility, so that learners have the ability to choose their learning trajectories and programmes, and 
thereby choose their own paths in life according to their talents and interests. 
Accordingly, UGC has framed the Curriculum and Credit Framework for Undergraduate 
Programmes which promotes holistic and multidisciplinary education. It allows students to explore 
different subjects in the first year and provides an opportunity to continue with the same subject or change 
of subject at the end of 2nd semester. All universities and colleges have been requested to adopt 
Curriculum and Credit Framework for Undergraduate Programmes 
Also, National Credit Framework jointly developed by University Grants Commission (UGC), All 
India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), National Council for Vocational Education & Training 
(NCVET), National Institute of Open Schooling(NIOS), Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), 
National Council of Education, Research & Training (NCERT), Directorate General of Training (DGT), 
Ministry of Education (MoE) and Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship(MSDE) is a 
comprehensive credit framework encompassing elementary, school, higher and vocational education and 
training incorporating creditization of various dimensions of learning i.e. academics, vocational skills and 
Experiential learning including relevant experience and proficiency/professional levels acquired. It 
encompasses qualifications frameworks as prescribed in National Higher Education Qualifications 
Framework (NHEQF), National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) and National Curriculum 
Framework (NCF), thereby providing broad-based multi-disciplinary / inter-disciplinary, holistic 
education with flexible curricula, creative combination of subjects, multiple pathways, establishing 
equivalence, facilitate national and international mobility. 
Several other initiatives to ensure flexibility have been taken such as setting up of Academic Bank 
of Credit, Guidelines for Multiple Entry and Exit in Academic Programmes offered in the HEIs to pave 
the way for seamless student mobility, between or within degree-granting HEIs and facilitate students to 

15 
 
choose their learning trajectory; Guidelines for pursuing two Academic Programmes simultaneously to 
facilitate multiple pathways to learning involving both formal and non-formal education modes trajectory; 
Curriculum and Credit Framework for Undergraduate Programs to facilitate flexibility to move from one 
discipline of study to another, one institution to another, switch to alternative modes of learning (offline, 
ODL, and Online learning, and hybrid modes of learning). 
Further recommendation of the Committee 
The Committee had specifically recommended that the Design Your Degree programme be 
adopted in other HEIs in the country. The Ministry’s response has neglected to express the extent 
to which this has been followed. The Committee therefore, suggest the Ministry to share a 
compliance report regarding the same at the earliest.  
Recommendation  
3. The Committee is of the view that under the Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) 
Scheme, strategic funding to higher educational institutions based on critical appraisal of State’s higher 
educational plans which describe each State’s strategy to address issues of equity, access and excellence 
in higher education can go a long way in pushing NEP’s aims. Key features of the Scheme like up-
gradation of existing autonomous colleges to universities, conversion of colleges to cluster colleges with 
revamping the curriculum, skill development, examination reform, upgrading institutions to higher level 
and strategic funding should be the special focus of the UGC. 
(Para 4.10.5 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 Under the Scheme of Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA), a total number of 208 
Universities have been approved for support under various components. The third phase of Rashtriya 
Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) has been approved in the form of Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha 
Abhiyan (PM-USHA) with an outlay of Rs. 12926.10 crore for the period 2023-24 to 2025-26.  
An amount of Rs. 5,613.12Crore approved for 440 projects by the 1st and 2nd PAB of PM-USHA. 
So far, 31 States/ UTs signed MoU under PM-USHA. 
As per the guidelines of the scheme of Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA), 
for each component, various criteria have been given on the basis of which scoring of the proposals can 
be done. Among the list of such indicators, percentage of faculty positions filled in regular mode are 
included where institutions with more than 75% positions filled will get the highest score under the 
components of Multi-Disciplinary Education and Research Universities (MERU) and Grants to 
Strengthen Universities. Institutions with more than 85% positions filled will get the highest score under 
the component of Grants to Strengthen Colleges. However, other institutions which have lesser faculty 
positions filled are also eligible under the components but will get their corresponding score. Currently 
there is no proposal under consideration to change this criterion. 
Further recommendation of the Committee 
The Committee’s recommendations had called for “up-gradation of existing autonomous 
colleges to universities, conversion of colleges to cluster colleges with revamping the curriculum, 
skill development, examination reform, upgrading institutions to higher level. Given the PM-USHA 
Scheme’s budget allocations, it doesn’t appear that current funding is sufficient to meet these goals. 
Therefore, an enhanced budget is necessary to meet the goals of the NEP in higher education. 
Furthermore, as mentioned, only rewards the HEIs have adequate staff and enable them to make 
even greater investments at a time when there is a need for broader-based investments across the 

16 
 
spectrum of HEIs. The Committee therefore, recommends that a parallel scheme to support HEIs, 
particularly those in Aspirational districts and catering to marginalised communities, with faculty 
recruitment and other investments should be formulated. The Committee also desires that details 
on the States/UTs which have not signed the PM-USHA MoU and what action the Ministry has 
taken to support HEIs in such states should be furnished at the earliest for its consideration.  
Recommendation  
4. The Committee hopes that the steps that the Department is taking as per NEP will be able to 
actively enhance engagement and find a connect with the industry and Higher Educational Institutions 
(HEIs), through which they can experiment, pitch ideas and deploy them bringing a close alignment in the 
practices of academia thereby synchronizing innovation and research with the need of the time and 
industry to achieve objective of real change. 
(Para 4.10.6 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 To benefit for India’s demographic dividend, the focus is on making Indian population skill ready 
by enhancing greater linkages between industry and academia. To this effect, guidelines on ‘Professor of 
Practice’ through which industry experts are being engaged with HEIs in developing courses and 
curriculum to meet the industry as well as societal needs. A portal to facilitate engagement of Professor of 
Practice in HEIs has been developed. Under this, 15560 domain experts across 23 domains and 465 HEIs 
have registered on the portal. 696 PoPs have been appointed by 422 HEIs. MoUs have been signed with 
leading companies such as CISCO/ IBM/ Meta/ Adobe/ Microsoft/Sales force to create industry aligned 
courses. 
SWAYAM Courses are designed and delivered by faculty members from the best institutions 
(CUs, IITs, IIMs), ensuring a high standard of education. Most of the SWAYAM Courses are of 1 to 4 
Credits, and are aligned to National Credit Framework for online learning courses.  
UGC has notified (Credit Framework for Online Learning Courses through Study Webs of Active 
Learning for Young Aspiring Minds) Regulations, 2021 on 25th March, 2021. Through these regulations, 
which now facilitate an institution to allow up to 40% (forty per cent.) of the total courses being offered in 
a particular programme in a semester through the online learning courses offered through SWAYAM 
Platform. The credits/marks obtained by the candidate enrolled in universities for SWAYAM Certificate 
will be counted in the transcript of the Candidate, only if the University has adopted MOOCs Courses 
offered on SWAYAM Platform for Credit Transfer as per the UGC (Credit Framework for Online 
Learning Courses through Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds) Regulations, 2021. 
SWAYAM+ has also been launched 27.02.2024 which is the extended arm of the SWAYAM 
Platform to offer the Industry aligned credit courses curated and delivered by Industry Professionals, 
enabling Industry Academia Collaboration. More than 1.10 lakh students across 231 courses are 
registered on the platform; SWAYAM Plus has MoUs with 54 Industry Partners covering emerging areas 
such as Artificial Intelligence, Manufacturing, Healthcare etc. More than 11,500 Internships also offered 
on the platform in collaboration with internshala. 
Further recommendation of the Committee 
The Committee notes the various steps taken by the Ministry to support industry-academia 
participation. It further notes that many of these initiatives however center on digital platforms and 
learning. Such a reliance on digital learning requires substantial and regular quality checks and 
impact assessments to ensure these interventions are having the anticipated effect on students. The 

17 
 
Committee desires that the Ministry should share a report of any assessments or feedback 
gathering that has been conducted on the platforms mentioned in its response for its consideration.  
Recommendation  
5. The Committee appreciates the manner in which the NEP 2020 places thrust on developing a 
student’s ‘Creative Potential’ based on higher-order cognitive capacities and to cultivate innovation and 
creativity in learners through industry-institution linkages and collaborative programme. Noting that the 
NEP prioritizes research and innovation with financial commitment to academic research, the Committee 
observes that promoting thought-provoking research is a pre-requisite for outstanding education and will 
surely transform India into a vibrant knowledge society. 
(Para 4.10.8 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 NEP 2020 inter-alia envisions a complete overhaul and re-energising of the higher education 
system to provide high-quality higher education, with equity and inclusion. One of its visions is to 
develop culture of research and innovation in India by establishing a National Research Foundation to 
fund outstanding peer-reviewed research and to actively seed research in universities and colleges. To 
propel Bharat towards scientific & technology leadership Anusandhan National Research Foundation 
(ANRF) has been set up under ANRF Act 2023 under Deptt. of Science & Technology. 
Also, UGC has finalized guidelines on Sustainable and Vibrant University-Industry Linkage 
System for Indian Universities. UGC has also requested all the Higher Education Institutions in its 
purview to take necessary action for the implementation of the guidelines in letter and spirit. 
Further recommendation of the Committee 
The Committee notes the setting up the ANRF to support research and innovation in higher 
education. However, it is concerned by the ANRF’s limited focus on science, technology, 
agriculture, and health technology. The Committee’s recommendation on support research was 
broad-based in its spirit, and included humanities and social sciences research which play an 
extremely important role in social, cultural, and economic progress. Therefore, the Committee 
recommends a parallel initiative to support humanities and social sciences research in higher 
education.  
Recommendation  
6. The Committee is of the view that proper involvement of the student community, incorporation of 
their feedback and suggestions towards the changes proposed in NEP will help institutions in orienting 
students faster and in a more effective way which will be helpful in creating institutional mechanisms to 
handle student’s queries on issues such as Academic Bank of Credits (ABC), Multiple Entry and Exit 
system and generate beneficial results in terms of acceptance and smoother implementation. In the early 
stages the learning has to be a both way process for a substantive evolution and successful 
implementation. 
(Para 4.10.14 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
 Government has been undertaking comprehensive consultation process with the stake holders after 
announcement of NEP, 2020 to address various issues.  

18 
 
UGC has announced NEP-SAARTHI – Student Ambassador for Academic Reforms in 
Transforming Higher Education in India with a view to bring students together as active participants in 
implementing NEP 2020.  Through NEP SAARTHI, the UGC aims to foster an environment where 
students can engage meaningfully with the reforms undertaken by the UGC. 
Presently, 855 NEP SAARTHIs from 309 Higher Educational Institutions have been selected.  
The list of the NEP SAARTHIs has been posted on the website. 
Further recommendation of the Committee 
The Committee notes the identification of the NEP Saarthis as a positive development in 
implementing the NEP. The Committee desires that the Ministry should share a report on the 
activities undertaken by the NEP Saarthis and would recommend the use of the NEP Saarthis to 
collect feedback on the implementation of the NEP.  
Recommendation  
7. Taking note of some of the observations of IRMA, the Committee is of the view that the successful 
implementation of initiatives to enhance access to education for marginalized communities is not only a 
moral imperative but also essential for the inclusive and sustainable development so that education 
becomes a powerful tool for uplifting all segments of society, regardless of their socio-economic status or 
background. The Committee, therefore, recommends for implementation of certain specific initiatives 
aimed at enhancing access to education for marginalized communities in accordance with the National 
Education Policy (NEP) 2020 so that its thrust on inclusivity and equitability for all segments of society 
gets requisite boost:  
i.  Comprehensive Awareness Campaigns: Launch comprehensive awareness campaigns 
targeting marginalized communities to inform them about the importance of education and 
the opportunities provided by the NEP 2020. These campaigns should be conducted in 
local languages and dialects, utilizing various media channels including television, radio, 
print, and social media. Collaboration with local community leaders and organizations to 
maximize outreach would also be helpful.  
ii.  Infrastructure Development: Invest in buildings and upgrading educational infrastructure 
in underserved areas, with particular focus on remote villages and urban slums. Ensure 
that schools are accessible, safe, and well-equipped to provide quality education. Allocate 
sufficient funds to address the specific needs of schools catering to marginalized 
communities.  
iii.  Teacher Training and Recruitment: Develop specialized training programs for teachers 
who work in marginalized communities. These programs should emphasize inclusive and 
culturally sensitive teaching methods, as well as provide incentives to attract qualified 
educators to these areas. Implement a transparent and efficient teacher recruitment 
process that prioritizes diversity.  
iv.  Scholarship and Financial Support: Establish a robust scholarship and financial support 
system to mitigate economic barriers to education. Scholarships should be designed to 
address the unique needs of marginalized communities, including those from economically 
disadvantaged backgrounds, scheduled castes, scheduled tribes, and other vulnerable 
groups. Streamline the application process to make it user-friendly and accessible.  
v.  Digital Inclusivity: Recognize the importance of digital education in the current context 
and work towards providing marginalized communities with access to digital resources. 

19 
 
Equip schools with computer labs and ensure affordable internet connectivity in these 
areas. 
vi.  Develop and distribute educational content tailored to local needs and languages.  
vii.  Community Engagement: Encourage active involvement of the local community in the 
education process. Establish Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs) and involve them in 
institution decision-making. Promote community-driven initiatives to support education, 
such as adult literacy programs and community libraries.  
viii.  Monitoring and Evaluation: Implement a robust monitoring and evaluation system to track 
the progress and impact of initiatives aimed at enhancing access to education for 
marginalized communities. Regularly collect data on enrollment, attendance, and learning 
outcomes, disaggregated by demographic factors, and disseminate it to identify areas 
needing improvement.  
ix.  Policy Adaptation: Continuously review and adapt policies to address the evolving needs 
and challenges faced by marginalized communities. Establish a feedback mechanism that 
allows stakeholders from these communities to provide input and suggestions for policy 
improvements.  
x.  Collaboration and Partnerships: Foster collaborations with Non-Governmental 
Organizations (NGOs), civil society organizations, and international agencies that have 
expertise in promoting education for marginalized communities. Leverage their resources 
and knowledge to enhance the effectiveness of education initiatives.  
xi.  Research and Innovation: Encourage research and innovation in the field of education for 
marginalized communities. Support studies that identify best practices and innovative 
approaches to address the unique challenges faced by these communities in accessing 
quality education. 
(Para 4.10.17-18 of the 356th Report of the Committee) 
Action Taken 
(i)  A number of outreach activities have been undertaken for awareness about National 
Education Policy 2020 by different implementing and regulatory bodies under Ministry of 
Education. Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education organized a short 
Video competition on the implementation of NEP, titled "NEP ki Samajh" from 
15.06.2023 to 14.07.2023, aiming to encourage young people to tap into their creativity to 
compose and submit short videos about their experiences with NEP 2020. 
(ii)  Samagra Shiksha scheme is an integrated scheme for school education covering the entire 
gamut from pre-school to class XII as a continuum. The scheme not only provides support 
for the implementation of the RTE Act but has also been aligned with the 
recommendations of NEP 2020 to ensure that all children have access to quality education 
with an equitable and inclusive classroom environment which should take care of their 
diverse background, multilingual needs, different academic abilities and make them active 
participants in the learning process. 
The major interventions, across all levels of school education, under the Samagra Shiksha scheme 
are: (a) Early Childhood Care and Education (b) Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (c) Universal 
Access including Infrastructure Development and Retention; (d) RTE Entitlements including uniforms, 
textbooks etc. (e) Quality and Innovation (f) Financial support for Teacher Salary (g) Appointment of 
language Teachers (h) Gender and Equity (i) Inclusive Education (j) Strengthening of Teacher Education 

20 
 
Institutions and Training (k) Vocational Education (l) ICT and Digital Initiatives (m) Sports and Physical 
Education (n) Monitoring and Programme Management and (o) National Component. 
In order to meet the RTE norms and to minimize the gaps in Schools, the Central Government, 
through integrated centrally sponsored scheme of Samagra Shiksha, provides support to the States and 
UTs for creation of school infrastructure facilities and opening/ upgradation of schools as per gaps 
identified from school mapping. As per norms of the Samagra Shiksha scheme, the annual plan are 
prepared by the States and UTs as per their requirements/priority and is reflected in their respective 
Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B) Proposals. These plans are then appraised and 
approved/estimated by the Project Approval Board (PAB) in the Department of School Education and 
Literacy in consultation with the States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial norms of the 
scheme and physical and financial progress of the State for the interventions approved earlier. 
(iii)  With regard to Teacher Education and Training, All 613 functional DIETs in the country 
will be upgraded into DIETs of Excellence in a phased manner in the next five years, 
through Samagra Shiksha at an estimated cost of ₹ 9,195/- crore. The scheme started with 
125 DIETs in FY 2023-24 with an estimated outlay of ₹ 921.62 crores. 
Also, NCTE has prepared Integrated Teacher Education Programme Curriculum Framework and 
Stage Specific Pedagogy Courses. Recognition granted to 42 institutions including IITs, NITs, RIEs, 
IGNOU and Government Colleges for the Academic Session 2023-24. 
Further, National Professional Standards for Teachers (NPST) guiding document has been 
launched on 9th March 2024. It outlines the competencies that teachers should possess to effectively 
perform their roles. 
Bluebook on National Mission for Mentoring has been launched on 9th March 2024. It underlines 
the importance of short and long-term mentoring/professional support. 
Digital Teacher Training leveraging DIKSHA infrastructure has enabled capability building at a National 
scale. 42 lakh teachers have completed 18 courses for NISHTHA (Elementary Level), 7.97 lakh teachers 
have completed 68 courses for NISHTHA (Secondary Level), 12.97 lakh teachers have completed 12 
courses NISHTHA (FLN) and 1.26 lakh teachers are undergoing 6 courses for NISHTHA (ECCE). 
Also ‘Capacity Building on Specific Learning Disabilities’ is conceptualized under the aegis of the 
Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Program (MMTTP) by the Department of Higher Education, 
Ministry of Education. It is part of the regular capacity-building program for faculty and institutions as 
envisioned in the National Education Policy 2020. This program focuses on specific learning disabilities, 
where resource persons/experts dealing with the various kinds of learning disabilities equip the 
institutions with the capacity to foster inclusion of students with SLDs in their institutions effectively. The 
program includes different sessions like Orientation Session, Sensitization Session, Masterclasses for each 
department, In-Person Zone-wise Workshops, Monitoring of Implementation, and Conclusion of the 
Phase. 
The First Cycle of the program was conducted from January to July 2024 in which a cohort of 27 
Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) participated in the program including Central Universities, IITs, 
IIITs, IIMs, IISERs, SPAs, and NITs. More than 400 faculty members from different departments of these 
institutions benefited. Recently, the Second Cycle of the CBSLD Program commenced with a new set of 
44 identified HEIs from August 2024 onwards. 
Also to develop leadership skills in the faculty at all level of Higher Education program like 
‘Nurturing Future Leadership Program’ is being conducted by the top IIMs / IITs. Similarly ‘Academic 

21 
 
Leadership Program’ targeting Vice- Chancellors/Directors/Heads Universities/Institutions have been 
rolled out.   
(iv)  The Union Cabinet vide its decision dated 19.01.2022, conveyed vide Cabinet Secretariat 
letter No. 2/CM/2022(i) dated 28.01.2022 approved continuation of the Scheme –Student 
Financial Aid (Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsanhan [PM-USP] Yojana” till 
31.03.2026 or till further review, whichever is earlier, comprising of 3 Central Sector sub- 
schemes namely - 
a)  PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students; aims 
to address the needs of marginalized communities by offering scholarships to students from 
reserved categories and economically weaker sections. The application process is streamlined 
through the National Scholarships Portal (NSP), with online verification by the institute and the 
State Higher Education Department. 
b)  PM-USP Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu &Kashmir and Ladakh; extends 
reservation benefits to various categories such as SC, ST, socially and economically backward 
classes, and economically weaker sections. The application process is managed through the 
AICTE online portal, ensuring real-time monitoring, transparency, and ease of process. 
c)  PM-USP Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme and Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for 
Education Loan; focuses on providing financial assistance to students, including minorities, 
SCs/STs, women, and disabled individuals, to facilitate access to professional higher education. 
The ceiling for education loans covered under the scheme has been raised to Rs. 10 lakhs from the 
financial year 2022-23. Disbursement of interest subsidy claims is carried out through Direct 
Benefit Transfer (DBT) into students' education loan accounts, and the application process is 
facilitated through an online portal managed by Canara Bank, the nodal bank for this purpose. 
Recently Union Cabinet approved PM Vidyalaxmi scheme to provide financial support to 
meritorious students so that financial constraints do not prevent any youth of India from pursuing quality 
higher education. A mission mode mechanism will facilitate and drive the extension of education loans to 
meritorious students who get admission in the top 860 quality higher educational institutions of the nation, 
translating to covering more than 22 lakh students every year. This special loan product will enable for 
collateral free, guarantor free education loans; made accessible through a simple, transparent, student-
friendly and entirely digital application process. Under this scheme loan amounts up to ₹ 7.5 lakhs will be 
provided a 75% credit guarantee by the Government of India, to support banks to expand coverage. 
Furthermore, for students with up to Rs. 8 lakhs annual family income, the scheme will also provide for 
3% interest subvention on loans up to Rs 10 lakh. This is in addition to the full interest subvention already 
offered to students with up to Rs. 4.5 lakhs annual family income. PM Vidyalaxmi will build on the scope 
and reach of initiatives taken over the last decade for maximizing access to quality higher education for 
the youth 
Apart from above, UGC is also implementing various scholarship/fellowship schemes to 
encourage students/research scholars to pursue higher education by providing financial assistance. The 
details of the schemes are as under: 
(a).  Junior Research Fellowship in Science, Humanities and Social Sciences: The objective of 
the scheme is to provide financial assistance to NET/JRF-qualified candidates to undertake 
advanced studies and research leading to M.Phil./Ph. D. Degree in Humanities and Social Sciences 
including Languages and Sciences. During the selection process of JRF candidates, the reservation 
policy as per the Govt. of India norms is followed, providing a fair chance to the marginal 
communities. 

22 
 
(b).  Savitribai Jyotirao Phule Single Girl Child Fellowship – The objective of the scheme is to 
provide financial assistance to single girl child of the family for pursuing Ph.D. There is no cap on 
the number of slots. All eligible applications are considered for fellowship. As per the eligibility 
criteria of the scheme, the students of reserved categories i.e. SC/ST/OBC and PWD (Persons with 
Disabilities) are given age relaxation of 5 years i.e. students up to the age of 40 years for general 
category and 45 years for reserved categories are eligible to apply. 
(c).  National Scholarship for Postgraduate Studies – The objective of the scheme is to provide 
financial assistance to Indian students leading to award of Postgraduate Degree. The slots are 
allocated as per Govt. of India reservation policy. Also, 30% slots are reserved for the women 
candidates. 
(d).  “Ishan Uday” Special Scholarship Scheme for North-Eastern Region–The scheme 
promotes higher education in the North-Eastern Region by providing financial assistance to 
students of the region pursuing Under Graduation. There are 10,000 slots under the scheme. The 
North-Eastern states have higher concentration of Scheduled Tribe population. Therefore, the 
scheme is providing benefit to the ST students by helping them in pursuing higher education. 
(v).  All the States and UTs have been advised to enter into an MoU/Agreement with BSNL and 
provide FTTH Internet connection to all the Government Schools which have computing devices. 
States / UTs have also been advised that the Internet Charges can be met from the following:

charges can be met from the recurring charges being released under Samagra 
Shiksha.  
•  For Schools in which ICT/ Smart Class room are not sanctioned under Samagra 
Shiksha and which have computing devices, internet charges can be met from the 
Management Monitoring Evaluation and Research (MMER) funds being released 
under Samagra Shiksha or can be met from any other State/UT Govt. funds. 
(vi)  The following major initiatives have been taken in order to make contents available to the

eliminating language barriers in the way of accessibility. These initiatives will benefit all students 
who face challenges in absence of availability of contents in regional/Indian languages including 
tribals and SEDGs. 
(a)  UGC to allow teaching-learning and examination in 22 Indian Languages 
(b)  UGC to make available books of all subjects in 22 Indian Languages 
(c)  100 Books for UG Students for Arts, Science and Humanities launched in 12 Indian

 A meeting was held on 30.01.2024 with all Regulatory Authorities and their representatives under

Action Taken 
 Multiple Entry and Exit (MEME) Guidelines issued on 27.07.2021 in conjunction with ABC 
Regulations, Guidelines on National Credit Framework (NCrF), Guidelines on National Higher Education 
Framework (NHEQF), Guidelines on Curriculum and Credit Framework for Undergraduate Programmes, 
Guidelines for Transforming Higher Education Institutions and Universities etc. aims to achieve 
objectives of NEP, 2020.  MEME Guidelines address several issues which were expected to be raised 
such as – in and out traffic in institutions; uneven geographical distribution of higher education 
institutions etc. 
After announcement of the NEP, 2020 and rolling out of MEME, HEIs are in the process of 
implementing the same and at present there is no empirical evidence to suggest that implementation of 
MEME will face hurdle. It is expected that with the passage of time and with more clarity emerging after 
rolling out of MEME with a dynamic regulatory intervention, the issue of exit and entry will even out and 
this transformative reform will be smoothly implemented in long term. 
Subsequently, UGC notified the National Credit Framework to enable the integration of vocational 
education with general education, multiple entry and exit etc. To develop SOPs for the implementation of 
NCrF and to remove difficulties in the implementation, a high-level committee was constituted by the 
Ministry of Education. The SOPs has been notified by UGC on 07.08.2024.  
For Operationalisation of National Credit Framework (NCrF) in Higher Education Standard 
Operating Procedure (SoP) has been issued.  The SOPs provides a clear guideline to facilitate the 
assignment, accumulation, storage, transfer, and redemption of such credits across school, higher, and 
vocational education and training and also advocates for multiple entry and exit points, recognition of 
prior learning, and work-embedded programs, enabling learners to acquire skills that integrate smoothly 
into formal education. The SOPs will empower educational institutions to serve as hubs for skill 
development, offering diverse learning pathways for students. 
Moreover, Government has been undertaking comprehensive consultation process with the stake 
holders after announcement of NEP, 2020 to address various issues. The recommendation of the Hon’ble 
Committee respectfully noted for further compliance.
